ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there is a grid composed of small squares with equal side lengths. Points $A$, $B$, $P$, and $Q$ are all located on the vertices of the square grid. The line segments $AB$ and $PQ$ intersect at point $E$. What is the value of $\tan\angle AEP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, let the side length of the small square be 1,\\
according to the grid characteristics, $\angle PQF=\angle CBF=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore PQ\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle QEB=\angle ABC$,\\
$\because \angle AEP=\angle QEB$,\\
$\therefore \angle AEP=\angle ABC$,\\
$\because AB=\sqrt{1^2+3^2}=\sqrt{10}$, $AC=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$, $BC=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore AC^2+BC^2=AB^2$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABC$ is a right triangle, and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \tan\angle ABC= \frac{AC}{BC}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
$\therefore \tan\angle AEP=\tan\angle ABC= \boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$.

method.method_draft: Synthetic parallel-and-right-triangle route: From the figure, take the small square side as 1 and name the top grid vertex above/right of A as C. Read from the grid that A is the left middle vertex, B is the bottom right vertex, P is the middle vertex one column right of A, and Q is the bottom vertex one column right of P. Segment PQ moves 1 square right and 1 square down, and segment CB moves 2 squares right and 2 squares down, so PQ ∥ CB. Since E is the intersection of AB and PQ, angle AEP equals the angle between AB and CB, i.e. angle ABC. Use grid distances: AB has horizontal/vertical offsets 3 and 1, so AB=sqrt(10); AC has offsets 1 and 1, so AC=sqrt(2); BC has offsets 2 and 2, so BC=2sqrt(2). Since AC^2+BC^2=AB^2, triangle ABC is right at C. Therefore tan(angle ABC)=AC/BC=sqrt(2)/(2sqrt(2))=1/2, hence tan(angle AEP)=1/2.

method.method_draft: Direct coordinate/vector route: Assign coordinates using the grid, for example with unit side length, x to the right and y upward: A=(0,1), B=(3,0), P=(1,1), Q=(2,0). The line AB has direction vector from E toward A parallel to A-B = (-3,1). The line PQ has direction vector from E toward P parallel to P-Q = (-1,1). The desired angle AEP is exactly the angle between these two ray directions. Compute tangent of the angle between vectors u=(-3,1) and v=(-1,1) by tan(theta)=|u_x v_y-u_y v_x|/(u·v). This gives |(-3)(1)-(1)(-1)| / [(-3)(-1)+1·1] = 2/4 = 1/2. Thus tan angle AEP=1/2.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, there is a grid composed of small squares with equal side lengths. Points $A$, $B$, $P$, and $Q$ are all located on the vertices of the square grid. The line segments $AB$ and $PQ$ intersect at point $E$. What is the value of $\tan\angle AEP$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, let the side length of the small square be 1,\\
according to the grid characteristics, $\angle PQF=\angle CBF=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore PQ\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle QEB=\angle ABC$,\\
$\because \angle AEP=\angle QEB$,\\
$\therefore \angle AEP=\angle ABC$,\\
$\because AB=\sqrt{1^2+3^2}=\sqrt{10}$, $AC=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$, $BC=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore AC^2+BC^2=AB^2$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABC$ is a right triangle, and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \tan\angle ABC= \frac{AC}{BC}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
$\therefore \tan\angle AEP=\tan\angle ABC= \boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$

Point A is at the middle grid point on the left boundary, point B is at the lower-right corner grid point, point P is at the middle grid point one square to the right of A, and point Q is on the bottom side and is the grid point one square to the lower right of P. Segment AB and segment PQ intersect at E. Additionally take the top-side grid point one square to the upper right of A in the figure as C; then from C to B along the grid direction is 2 squares to the right and 2 squares downward; from P to Q is 1 square to the right and 1 square downward.
Reasoning: Let the side length of a small square be 1. From the grid displacements in the figure, the direction of PQ is 1 to the right and 1 downward, and the direction of CB is 2 to the right and 2 downward, so PQ ∥ CB. Because E is on AB and E is also on PQ, ∠AEP is equal to the angle formed by line AB and line CB, namely ∠ABC. From grid distances: the horizontal and vertical displacements of AB are respectively 3 and 1, so AB = sqrt(3^2+1^2)=sqrt(10); the horizontal and vertical displacements of AC are respectively 1 and 1, so AC=sqrt(2); the horizontal and vertical displacements of BC are respectively 2 and 2, so BC=sqrt(8)=2sqrt(2). Therefore AC^2+BC^2=2+8=10=AB^2, and triangle ABC is a right triangle at C. Thus tan∠ABC=AC/BC=sqrt(2)/(2sqrt(2))=1/2. Therefore tan∠AEP=1/2.
